body:
## Finding (unaddressed PR review comment)

On PR #8025 (`fix(power-guard): detect dead systemd-inhibit child, re-engage loudly`, for issue #6534), CodeRabbit raised a stability finding that was never fixed or replied to:

> **Keep sampling while a stalled child is reaped.** If `systemd-inhibit` does not exit promptly, `release()` can block the loop for about 10 seconds. This delays the next sample or the confirmed sleep command. Handle stalled reaping without blocking sampling, and confirm inhibitor release before issuing sleep.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025#discussion_r4511572429 (comment id 4511572429)
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-09T10:10:56Z
- Location: `nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`, `Inhibitor._reap()` / `release()` (lines 153–175 at PR head)

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-10) and has no replies — the CodeRabbit comment is the only comment in the thread.
- PR #8025's head is unchanged since the comment: the only commit is `2a6abfda8194eb944894b5fc647778f82aa977f5` (2026-11-09T10:04:21Z, before the comment). No fix commit followed.
- The PR is still open and the comment is more than 24 hours old, so the open-PR grace rule is expired.
- No existing issue covers this (searched open/recently-closed issues for power-guard / inhibitor / release on 2026-11-10; issue #6534 covers dead-child detection, not reap blocking).

## Still-live evidence (PR head `2a6abfda81`, read 2026-11-10)

`nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`:

- `_reap()` (lines 153–175) waits synchronously: `proc.wait(timeout=5)`, and on timeout escalates to `kill()` and waits another 5 seconds — up to ~10 seconds of blocking in the caller.
- `release()` calls `_reap()` synchronously (line 253), and `main()` calls `release()` inline in the sampling loop — both on the recovery path (line 292) and, critically, on the confirmed-sleep path (lines 310–312), where the sleep command is only issued after `release()` returns. A stalled child therefore delays an already-confirmed emergency sleep by up to ~10 seconds on a critical battery, and delays every other sample while reaping.

Note the interaction with the companion finding from the same review (release forgetting a still-running child): the fix must keep sampling/reaping from blocking the loop **without** dropping the requirement that inhibitor release is confirmed before the sleep command is issued.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reaping a stalled `systemd-inhibit` child no longer blocks the sampling loop for the full double-wait; sampling continues while reaping is pending, **and** the confirmed-sleep path still does not issue the sleep command until inhibitor release is confirmed; **or** the current behavior is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.
- The existing timeout and kill-escalation safeguards are preserved.
- Regression coverage: a fake child that ignores terminate/kill exercises the non-blocking reap path in `test_power_guard.py`.
